name: OPS And Ever
classification_notes: A six-weight sans with full italics built primarily for expressive, literary display settings rather than neutral text.
summary: A six-weight sans with full italics, one of OPS Type's newest releases shown through literary, introspective specimen text.
description: OPS And Ever runs from Thin to Black with matching italics at every weight, giving it a fuller range than most of OPS Type's other, more conceptual releases. The specimen leans on personal, narrative text rather than commercial copy, in keeping with the foundry's usual tone. An Ultra weight extends the family further.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type presents OPS And Ever through literary passages exploring personal narrative and introspection, showing the family's range across its weights.

name: OPS And Ever Ultra
classification_notes: The heaviest cut of OPS And Ever, built specifically for display use at the top of the family's weight range.
summary: The Ultra-weight extension of OPS And Ever, built for heavier display use than the core family covers.
description: OPS And Ever Ultra pushes the parent family's weight range further still, aimed squarely at headline and display settings rather than text. It shares the family's italic across its heaviest cuts. A companion release rather than a standalone design.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type extends OPS And Ever with an Ultra weight for heavier display use, keeping the family's literary specimen voice.

name: OPS Facitype
classification_notes: Modelled directly on the mechanics of Arabic-script typewriters built for Iran, Iraq and Egypt, this is a typewriter-style monospace revival.
summary: A single-weight typewriter revival modelled on the specialist machines built for Arabic-script typing.
description: OPS Facitype takes its reference from typewriters engineered for Arabic-script keyboards used in Iran, Iraq and Egypt, translating that mechanical history into a Latin monospace. It's built as a conceptual, archival piece rather than a general text face, suited to labels, forms and manuscript-style layouts.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type frames Facitype around the specially engineered Arabic-script typewriters used in Iran, Iraq and Egypt, capturing that mechanical typesetting history for labels, tabulations, forms and manuscripts.

name: OPS Kappla
classification_notes: Conceptual, essay-driven specimen framing rather than a documented text role places this among OPS Type's experimental display releases.
summary: An experimental single-weight display face, presented through conceptual rather than commercial specimen text.
description: OPS Kappla is one of OPS Type's more conceptual releases, given no formal design brief on the foundry's own site beyond evocative specimen phrases. Single weight, no italic. Best treated as a display face for projects that want an unplaceable, slightly off-kilter character.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type presents Kappla through fragmented, conceptual specimen phrases rather than a conventional design description.

name: OPS Placard
designer: Jan Egbers, Matthias Kreutzer and Jens Schildt
classification_notes: Inspired by office typewriting and secretarial practice, with a full italic and bold range, this reads as a text-capable conceptual grotesque.
summary: A conceptual grotesque drawing on office typing practice, with enough range in weight and italic for actual text use.
description: OPS Placard takes its conceptual grounding from secretarial and office typing practice, framing text composition as a political and bodily act. Four styles, including a bold and italic, make it more usable for running text than most of the foundry's single-weight experiments.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type's specimen for Placard draws on office work and secretarial practice, exploring the body as a political construct through typewriter-style text composition.

name: OPS Used Future
designer: Jan Egbers, Matthias Kreutzer and Jens Schildt
classification_notes: A single-weight face presented through philosophical specimen text about placeholder content, placing it as a conceptual display release.
summary: A conceptual display face questioning the status of placeholder and overlooked text.
description: OPS Used Future is presented through a specimen that asks what status a redundant, overlooked placeholder text actually has, in keeping with the foundry's habit of framing typefaces as small essays. Single weight, no italic. A display piece for projects with a similarly questioning tone.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type frames Used Future around the question of what exact status a redundant, ignored, possibly overlooked placeholder text holds.

name: OPS Noise Abroad
designer: Jan Egbers, Matthias Kreutzer and Jens Schildt
classification_notes: Published in a condensed cut without a corresponding standard width, this sits as a condensed display sans.
summary: A condensed display sans, one of OPS Type's single-style experimental releases.
description: OPS Noise Abroad is issued only as a Condensed cut, without the foundry publishing a separate standard width. Single style, no italic. Another entry in OPS Type's run of small, conceptually framed releases.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type lists Noise Abroad as a condensed release within its collection of experimental typefaces.

name: OPS Grotesko
classification_notes: A single-weight grotesque presented alongside essays on typography's pedagogical history, positioning it within the foundry's design-education conversation.
summary: A single-weight grotesque presented through essays on typography's role in design education rather than a conventional specimen.
description: OPS Grotesko skips the usual promotional specimen copy in favour of contextual essays about typography's pedagogical history, in line with OPS Type's academic bent. Single weight, no italic. Best read as a working grotesque with an unusually thoughtful presentation.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type presents Grotesko through essays on typography's pedagogical history and its role in design culture rather than a conventional foundry description.

name: OPS Favorite
designer: Jan Egbers, Matthias Kreutzer and Jens Schildt
classification_notes: A four-style grotesque with bold and italic cuts, demonstrated across display and editorial contexts, gives it enough range for general text use.
summary: A versatile four-style grotesque demonstrated across both display and editorial settings.
description: OPS Favorite is one of the more straightforwardly usable typefaces in OPS Type's catalogue, with a regular, bold and matching italics rather than a single conceptual cut. The specimen shows it working in both display and editorial contexts. A safer choice than most of the foundry's other releases.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type presents Favorite through extended text passages that demonstrate the typeface's versatility across display and editorial contexts.

name: OPS Capitalis Brutalis
classification_notes: Framed by the foundry around Dada aesthetics and an anti-communicative approach to language, this sits as an experimental brutalist display face.
summary: A bold, brutalist display face framed by the foundry through Dada aesthetics rather than conventional legibility.
description: OPS Capitalis Brutalis is presented through conceptual language about Dada and a deliberately different aesthetic of language, rather than as a neutral working typeface. Bold weight only, no italic. Built for identity and editorial projects with an experimental, anti-corporate stance.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type frames Capitalis Brutalis through Dada aesthetics, presenting it as embodying a different aesthetic of language rather than conventional communication.

name: OPS Past Perfect
classification_notes: A single-weight grotesque shown through fragmented specimen phrases rather than a formal description, in keeping with the foundry's conceptual releases.
summary: A single-weight conceptual grotesque, shown through fragmented rather than descriptive specimen text.
description: OPS Past Perfect is documented mostly through its own specimen phrasing rather than a stated design brief, consistent with OPS Type's tendency to let the typeface speak through use rather than marketing copy. Single weight, no italic.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type presents Past Perfect through design specimens showing letterforms and contextual text samples rather than a formal foundry description.

name: OPS Cubic
designer: Jan Egbers, Matthias Kreutzer and Jens Schildt
classification_notes: A four-style grotesque framed around the mechanisation of movable type and assembly-line production, with enough weight and italic range for text use.
summary: A four-style grotesque conceptually tied to the mechanisation of movable type and assembly-line production.
description: OPS Cubic ties its specimen text to the industrial history of movable type, drawing a line from typesetting to assembly-line manufacturing. Regular, bold and matching italics give it enough range for genuine text use rather than a single conceptual cut.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type frames Cubic around the assemblage of text using moveable type, connecting it to the shift in thinking that gave way to assembly-line factories.

name: OPS Restructional Text
classification_notes: Described by the foundry as a text typeface with a standard and a 'cranked' variant, this is classified as a text serif built for reading rather than display.
summary: A text-oriented serif with an unusual 'Cranked' variant alongside its regular cut.
description: OPS Restructional Text is one of the few OPS Type releases explicitly billed as a text face rather than a display or conceptual piece. The Cranked variant offsets the design for a slightly skewed reading rhythm. Built for professional editorial use.
foundry_blurb: OPS Type describes Restructional Text as a curated typeface designed for contemporary typographic use, offered in Regular and Cranked variants.
